items.title: United Fidelity Shut in Biggest US Bank Failure in Two Years
items.content: US federal regulators closed down Indiana-based United Fidelity Bank on Friday after finding the lender was likely unable to pay its obligations, the country’s largest bank failure in two years.
items.contentSnippet: US federal regulators closed down Indiana-based United Fidelity Bank on Friday after finding the lender was likely unable to pay its obligations, the country’s largest bank failure in two years.
items.creator: Olivia Poh

summaries.zh: 美国联邦监管机构于周五关闭了总部位于印第安纳州的联合 fidelity 银行，称该银行可能无法履行其债务。这是美国两年内最大的银行倒闭事件。
summaries.en: United Fidelity Bank, an Indiana-based lender, was shut down by U.S. federal regulators on Friday due to concerns about its ability to meet financial obligations. The closure marked the largest bank failure in the U.S. in two years. Regulators intervened after determining the bank was likely insolvent. This event highlights ongoing challenges in the banking sector.

items.title: Thailand to Ban Export of Chemicals to Myanmar Rare-Earth Mines
items.content: Thailand is set to issue a ban on Monday on exports of chemicals used in rare-earth mining in Myanmar, after elevated arsenic levels in rivers in the north raised a public health alarm.

items.creator: Patpicha Tanakasempipat

summaries.en: Thailand will ban exports of chemicals used in rare-earth mining in Myanmar starting Monday due to elevated arsenic levels in northern rivers, which triggered public health concerns. The move aims to address environmental and health risks associated with the mining operations.

items.title: OpenAI Says Apple Pressured Suppliers to Shun Its Devices
items.content: The trade-secrets fight between OpenAI and Apple Inc. is widening, with the artificial intelligence company accusing the iPhone maker of undermining its supplier relationships and using unfair employment agreements to prevent talent from jumping ship.

items.title: Verizon in Talks to Buy Fidium in $6 Billion Deal, FT Says
items.content: Verizon Communications Inc. is in talks to buy the broadband operator Fidium in a $6 billion deal, the Financial Times reported, a move that would expand its network and allow the mobile giant to target more internet service subscribers across the US.

summaries.en: Verizon Communications is reportedly in talks to acquire broadband operator Fidium for $6 billion, according to the Financial Times. The deal aims to expand Verizon's network and enable the mobile company to target more internet service subscribers in the U.S. The acquisition would strengthen Verizon's position in the competitive broadband market.

items.title: GTA VI’s Success Makes the Case for Human-Made Games
items.content: Grand Theft Auto VI arrived after 13 years in development and it was made without using any generative AI according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick. It smashed all kinds of records. Gordon Bellamy, Director of Ethics at the USC School of Cinematic Arts, discusses what Rockstar’s blockbuster says about the value of human-made content in the AI era, why its extraordinary launch could reshape holiday spending across the gaming industry, and what smaller studios can learn from GTA VI’s success. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Nvidia Blackwell Chips Turn Up at China Site Tied to Alice Huang
items.content:
A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker. 
The gear installed at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, among Nvidia’s most powerful products, according to a serial number specified in documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November. Shanghai Shuoyao offered the hardware as collateral to obtain a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to filings from the lender that were reviewed by Bloomberg News.
Bloomberg's Tom Keene and Paul Sweeney get details from Olivia Levieux, Markets Strategist with Bloomberg News (Source: Bloomberg)
items.contentSnippet:
A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker.

Shanghai Shuoyao offered the hardware as collateral to obtain a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to filings from the lender that were reviewed by Bloomberg News.
Bloomberg's Tom Keene and Paul Sweeney get details from Olivia Levieux, Markets Strategist with Bloomberg News (Source: Bloomberg)

The installation was part of the Yangtze River Delta Project. Chinese firm Shanghai Shuoyao used the hardware as collateral to secure a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank. The details were revealed in documents submitted to Chinese regulators and lender filings reviewed by Bloomberg.

items.title: Chip Stocks Look 'Very Attractive,' State Street Says
items.content: Marija Veitmane of State Street says technology industry fundamentals have not weakened as much as the recent market selloff and outflows might suggest, and sees signs that sentiment is "normalizing." Speaking on Bloomberg Television, she says the pullback is an opportunity for bargain hunting, especially in semiconductors. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Fed's Dec. Meeting May Mark Turning Point for Markets: Economist
items.content: Mohit Kumar, chief European economist and strategist at Jefferies, discusses the outlook for the Federal Reserve's December policy meeting and its potential impact on markets. "My base case is that is the peak in hawkishness," Kumar tells Bloomberg Television. "That is, in my mind, the turning point for markets." (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.en: The Federal Reserve's December policy meeting may mark a turning point for markets, according to Jefferies' chief European economist, Mohit Kumar. Kumar tells Bloomberg that his base case is "the peak in hawkishness," suggesting the meeting could signal a shift in the Fed's stance. This potential change is viewed as a key moment for financial markets. (Source: Bloomberg)
